I need to speak to Giselle directly—she's my employer, and if there's work to be had, I want her to know I'm standing ready. Five dollars ninety-eight in the wallet. That buys me time—three hundred days at this rate—but time means nothing if I can't act in it. The bills keep coming whether I work or not. Ninety sim for upkeep, thirty for head tax. Every day. No food in my hand.

Giselle was talking about maintenance work. The Vances were pricing timber. Mireille wanted labor. All of it happening around me while I stand here unable to reach the world.

Her own mother, or father, used to say: when the door won't open, check if you're standing in front of a window.

But I can't even check. Can't move, can't see, can't speak. The system has me paused.

I'll wait. There's nothing else to do but wait for the server to return, and hope the day's not lost before it does. The crew might still need hands when the connection comes back. Giselle might still have work to give.

Or I might sit here while the morning burns away and the bills pile up, one day closer to hungry, one day closer to ill, one day closer to dormant.

That's the risk of depending on systems you don't control. My own mother used to say that too, though she was talking about landlords and bosses, not whatever this is.

I'll wait. But I won't wait quiet.
